title: Clear the user-level token blacklist on successful login so a credential change does not lock the account out
goal: RevokeUserTokens sets a user-level Redis key blacklist:<userID> with TTL AccessTokenTTL+1m, and TokenAuthMiddleware rejects every request while that key exists. Login never clears it, so after a password reset or a disable/enable cycle the user cannot get in for roughly sixteen minutes -- and the error is 401 token.expired.force, which reads like an expired session rather than a lockout. The fix is narrow by design: clear the user-level key only after authentication succeeds, and leave session-level revocation (blacklist:session:*) intact so tokens issued before the reset stay dead.
findings: F2 (P1): the user-level blacklist key set by RevokeUserTokens is never cleared at login, so resetting a password or toggling status locks the account out for about sixteen minutes with a misleading 401 token.expired.force.

out: Removing user-level revocation on password reset or disable
Clearing session-level blacklist entries at login
Changing AccessTokenTTL or refresh-token rotation policy

implementationNotes: Add an explicit ClearUserBlacklist (or equivalent) next to BlacklistUser rather than issuing a raw DEL from the login path, so the key format stays owned by one package.
Call it only after credentials verify and after GateSessionIssuance passes. Clearing earlier would let a failed login reset a lockout that a disable action just imposed.
Session-level revocation must survive: the requirement is 'the new session works, the old tokens do not', not 'everyone is forgiven'.
Cover the ordering with a test that disables a user, re-enables, logs in, and asserts both the successful login and the rejection of a token minted before the disable.

runtimeEvidence: reset password then log in immediately: 200 with a usable session
a token minted before the reset still returns 401 token.expired.force
Redis keyspace shows no residual blacklist:<userID> after the successful login

humanGates: Confirm the product expectation: this packet keeps old refresh tokens revoked after a password reset. A 'sign out every device' requirement is a different feature.
completionChecklist: Login clears the user-level blacklist only after successful authentication
Session-level revocation still rejects pre-change tokens
Immediate login after reset or re-enable succeeds
